_comment: Silero VAD v6.2 (16 kHz) per-tensor tolerances for compare_tensors.py.
Regime, identical for every number below:
model     models/silero-vad-v6.2/silero-vad-v6.2-F32.gguf (ALL_F32)
runtime   build/bin/transcribe-cli --backend cpu --threads 1
(transcribe_vad_run; production path, nothing injected)
reference silero-vad 6.2.3 (silero_vad.jit, sha256 e1122837...), torch
2.8.0, fp32, CPU, 1 thread, scored frame by frame exactly as
get_speech_timestamps does
host      macOS / arm64 (Apple M4), ggml CPU backend
cases     all 9 in tests/golden/silero_vad/silero-vad-v6.2.manifest.json
(speech, silence-heavy, noise, zh/ja, 2-speaker, music, 197 s)
Every tensor is stacked over all frames of the clip ([n_frames, ...]), so
max_abs is the worst frame of up to 6162 recurrent steps.
Recipe, per tensor, over all 9 cases:
finalized = max(1.5 * observed, provisional, 1e-6)
with provisional = 1e-4 * p99_abs (max) / 1e-5 * rms (mean) from the
reference dumps. Most entries keep the provisional budget: observed drift
is 5-50x below it.
WIDENED vs provisional (max_abs only):
enc.3.out   observed 1.917e-04 (ja) -> 2.876e-04 (provisional 2.563e-04)
dec.lstm_h  observed 8.541e-05 (ja) -> 1.282e-04 (provisional 9.707e-05)
Mechanism: fp32 reduction order. enc.3.out is a 192-term dot product
(3 taps x 64 channels) whose ReLU output reaches ~10 on loud frames.
The 1.917e-4 drift is about 201 fp32 ULPs at magnitude 10: accumulated reduction
error rather than a single rounding step. dec.lstm_h inherits it through
the 128-wide W_ih projection and the recurrence. mean_abs on both stays
under 30% of budget.
Drift sources: ggml's SIMD reduction order in the STFT (256-tap) and conv
matmuls versus PyTorch's oneDNN/Accelerate conv1d, and the decoder's
polynomial expf (sigmoid / tanh within 9e-8 absolute of exact, the same as
libm's sigmoid). The algebra is exact: an fp64 NumPy re-derivation of the
forward pass is closer to the C++ probabilities than to the reference's
(max |c++ - fp64| 3.3e-06 vs max |ref - fp64| 7.6e-06 over the cases).
vad.probs is the gate, together with exact speech-segment parity
(validate.py compares every segment's start / end sample against
get_speech_timestamps). Observed vad.probs max_abs 6.9e-06.
